newsitem.title: UK: Christian faces lashes for taking UAE Moslem wife.
newsitem.headline: Christian faces lashes for taking UAE Moslem wife.

text.p: Amnesty International said on Friday it was deeply concerned by reports a Christian man would be flogged in the United Arab Emirates on Saturday and faced a year in jail for marrying a Moslem woman.

Family members told Reuters that Elie Dib Ghalib, a 30-year-old Lebanese, was arrested in December 1995 in the eastern UAE oasis city of Al-Ain and would receive 39 lashes in a local prison because an Islamic court ruled his marriage was null and void and his marital relationship was immoral.

"(He) was allegedly beaten and flogged many times during his pre-trial detention and interrogation in Al-Ain police station, apparently in order to force him to sign a confession," the international human rights group said.
Under Islamic sharia law, a non-Moslem man is not allowed to marry a Moslem woman unless he converts to Islam.
"The organisation is also concerned that he appears to be a prisoner of conscience held on the grounds of his Christian religion and that he has allegedly been tortured," Amnesty International said.
The UAE embassy in London said it had no comment.
Ghalib's wife Mona, a UAE national studying in the United States, said she had been brushed off by her husband's lawyer when she called to ask what had happened after the trial on October 29.

"He was totally outraged because I was a Moslem and was married to a Christian," Mona, 25, told Reuters. "The lawyer just said to me: 'This man is no longer your husband. You have no right to be calling me.'"
Mona and Ghalib were married in June, 1995 in Lebanon, in what she said was a bid to avoid controversy over a mixed-religion marriage.
"Such a marriage is no problem in Lebanon, or in the United States, or anywhere else in the world," she said. "Why the heck are they making this problem?"
After the wedding, Mona returned to her studies in the United States and Ghalib went back to his job as restaurant manager at the Intercontinental Hotel in Al-Ain, Amnesty International said.

He was arrested a few months later, Mona said. "The authorities went to his place, turned it upside-down, found the marriage certificate and then went to his office at the Intercontinental. They took him from there," she said.

Amnesty International said it had written to UAE authorities in April expressing concern that Ghalib was being detained over his marriage and asked for clarification. It said it had not yet received a reply.
